questions.prompt: Which phrase best describes what Redis is?

options.text: A relational database that stores tables on disk
An in-memory key-value store that serves rich data structures over the network
A programming language for data processing
A file system optimized for large binary files

questions.explanation: Redis (REmote DIctionary Server) keeps data in memory and maps keys to rich data structures (strings, lists, hashes, sets, sorted sets, and more), accessed over the network.

questions.prompt: Why is each individual Redis command atomic?

options.text: Because Redis locks every key before writing to it
Because commands are executed one at a time in a single thread, so none can interleave
Because Redis runs every command inside a database transaction with rollback
Because clients coordinate with each other before sending commands

questions.explanation: Redis executes command logic in a single thread, running each command to completion before the next — so a single command can never be observed half-done.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Redis are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Redis can persist data to disk with RDB snapshots and/or the AOF
Redis can be used as a cache, a database, and a message broker
Redis is entirely single-threaded and never uses any other threads
A single slow command can block other clients

questions.explanation: Redis persists via RDB/AOF, plays all three roles, and blocks on slow commands (so avoid them). It is NOT entirely single-threaded — only command execution is; it uses extra threads for I/O and background work.

questions.prompt: Since Redis 8.0 (May 2025), which licensing statement is correct?

options.text: Redis is closed source with no source available
Redis is available under a choice of AGPLv3 (open source), RSALv2, or SSPLv1
Redis is only under the SSPL and is not open source
Redis returned to the BSD-3-Clause license

questions.explanation: Redis 8.0 added AGPLv3 (an OSI-approved open-source license) alongside the source-available RSALv2 and SSPLv1, making Redis tri-licensed. It did not return to BSD; Valkey is the BSD-licensed fork.

questions.prompt: The BSD-licensed fork of Redis 7.2.4, created under the Linux Foundation in 2024, is called ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Valkey was forked from Redis 7.2.4 after the March 2024 relicense and is governed by the Linux Foundation under the permissive BSD license.

questions.prompt: Match each store to the best short description.

pairs.right: In-memory data-structure store (cache, DB, and broker)

questions.explanation: Redis is a rich in-memory store; Memcached is a plain string cache; a relational database is durable and queryable; Valkey is the open-source fork of Redis.
